judged.title: SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) - ITS - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) Overview Directly to: 1. basic information Field of application The system enables the digital processing of business trip requests as well as the creation and submission of travel expense reports via the SAP Employee Self-Service (ESS). Who is it suitable for? Employees can use ESS. Responsibility Responsibility for the SAP FIORI apps is regulated as follows: The HR department is responsible for the content-related operation as well as access and the provision of training. The technical operation is ensured by ITS or HeHRZ Darmstadt. 2. short description Description The SAP ESS portal offers an end-to-end workflow for the approval of business trip requests and travel expense reports. The processes are digitized and handled via the web browser - including uploading evidence and automatic form creation. Since summer 2025, ESS has been accessed entirely via SAP FIORI. Alternatives There are currently no technical alternatives available. 3. main functions Functions • Create business trip request • Workflow & approval: multi-stage process - technical and financial review, automatic commitment of funds. • Travel expense report: transfer of application data, entry of actual costs, upload of receipts, selection of domestic and international scheme. • Status overview: Accessible overviews of travel requests, expense reports and their processing status. Possibility to correct, delete or change under certain conditions 4th deployment scenario Practical examples

top5.opening: Erasmus+ personal mobility for teaching purposes (STA) - UNI Erasmus+ personal mobility for teaching purposes (STA) Erasmus+ enables employees at the University of Kassel to spend time teaching at European partner universities. The University of Kassel has bilateral agreements with a number of European partner universities as part of the personal mobility for teaching purposes scheme. You also have the opportunity to complete a period of teaching abroad at a selected international partner university as part of the Erasmus+ worldwide scheme. You can find general information about the Erasmus+ programme here. • Ongoing professional and personal development for lecturers • To promote cooperation between the University of Kassel and its European partner universities • Offering students, who cannot take part in any mobility programme, the opportunity to continue their international studies through the expert knowledge of lecturers from European partner universities ("internationalisation at home") • Enhancing the content of the teaching materials and the specialist exchange and strengthening the cooperation with international colleagues • Developing joint study programmes and exchanging teaching materials and methods People eligible for funding • Professors and lecturers with a contractual relationship with the University of Kassel • Part-time teaching staff with service contracts • Emeritus professors and retired teaching staff • Research assistants • Personnel from foreign companies and organisations (can be invited to German universities for teachi

top5.opening: Ghana Permaculture Institute Empowerment program for Peasant farmersin Bono East Region - FORSCHUNG - Uni Kassel Ghana Permaculture Institute Empowerment program for Peasant farmersin Bono East Region General Information Empowerment Workshop Time: 7th-8th January 2021 Location: Paolo Hall, Ghana Permaculture Institute Workshop Organizer: Ghana Permaculture Institute Workshop Report Workshop Report: Download Contact us For further information, please write us an email Thematic focus This workshop is going to focus on peasant farmers in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana. Peasant farmers in this region face issues such as land litigation, how to acquire funding, Application of chemicals. Ghana Permaculture Institute will invite resource persons from various universities and Agricultural Departments in this region. These resource persons will educate participants on how to acquire a litigation free land, acquire loans or funding to expand their farming business and how produce organic farm produce. This workshop will invite 60 peasant farmers within the Brong Ahafo region and take them through lectures for two (2) days. Participants and resource persons will be given lunch and snacks and transportation fees to cover their travel expenses. judged.title: 4. project implementation - INTERN - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: 4. project implementation - INTERN - Uni Kassel 4. project implementation The content on this page was translated automatically. When carrying out externally funded research projects, care must be taken to ensure that only expenditure that is necessary to achieve the project objective - taking into account the budgetary principle of efficiency and economy - may be incurred. Which expenses are covered by this is usually determined by the approval in conjunction with the specific cost and financing plan of the funding application and the funding guidelines of the respective program. Please note that the information you provide in the project application is the basis for the approval of funds and forms the framework for the subsequent use of the funds during project implementation. Expenditure expressly rejected by the donor may not be incurred under any circumstances. In the case of expenditure that only becomes necessary in the course of project implementation and for which there is no approval within the framework of the existing financing plan, consultation with the donor is required in all cases. In order to avoid later complaints during audits by the donor, you should have such expenditure approved in writing. If it is not clear from an expenditure receipt why the procurement/travel etc. was necessary for the project or to achieve the project objective, a brief explanation should be included on the expenditure receipt. top5.opening: FAQ - UNI FAQ Here you can find answers to frequently asked questions that have come up in the context of applying for internal funding through the central research fund (ZFF). Yes, Kunsthochschule is a semi-autonomous faculty of the University of Kassel, and all members are therefore eligible to apply for all ZFF funding lines. The funding lines themselves restrict eligibility to certain career stages; this applies equally to all members of the university, including Kunsthochschule. Both funding lines are currently suspended due to the cuts in the higher education sector in Hesse, cf. the Presidential Board resolution P/685 of 15 Sept 2025 on the internal documents server. Contacting Research Support is not mandatory, but nevertheless advisable so as to gauge your chances of success. Besides the quality of your proposal, several other factors influence funding success, viz. the amount of funding still available, as the funding lines "Project" and "Co-op" have annual caps. When carrying out externally funded research projects, care must be taken to ensure that only expenditure that is necessary to achieve the project objective - taking into account the budgetary principle of efficiency and economy - may be incurred. Which expenses are covered by this is usually determined by the approval in conjunction with the specific cost and financing plan of the funding application and the funding guidelines of the respective program. Please note that the information you provide in the project application is the basis for the approval of funds and forms the framework for the subsequent use of the funds during project implementation. Expenditure expressly rejected by the donor may not be incurred under any circumstances. In the case of expenditure that only becomes necessary in the course of project implementation and for which there is no approval within the framework of the existing financing plan, consultation with the donor is required in all cases. In order to avoid later complaints during audits by the donor, you should have such expenditure approved in writing. If it is not clear from an expenditure receipt why the procurement/travel etc. was necessary for the project or to achieve the project objective, a brief explanation should be included on the expenditure receipt. top5.opening: Erasmus+ Cycling University of Kassel - FB14BAU - Uni Kassel Erasmus+ This page contains automatically translated content. Image: Simeon Uhl Erasmus+ is a mobility programme for students and staff. Our department launched this programme in 2023, establishing cooperations with four Erasmus+ partner regions: the Western Balkans (Albania), Sub-Saharan Africa (Ghana, Uganda, Ethiopia), Ukraine, Georgia, and the Caribbean (Trinidad and Tobago). The main objectives of the Erasmus+ mobility program include staff mobility for the exchange of academic and non-academic staff for professional development, job shadowing, study visits, and participation in workshops or seminars; the preparation and evaluation of mobility activities; the development of joint publications; and the initiation of externally funded projects. Student mobility focuses on individual research projects and work related to doctoral studies, dissertations, or laboratory work, utilizing a mobility simulator for personal research purposes (at the University of Kassel). For doctoral students, the program emphasizes the creation of joint publications and the initiation of externally funded projects. To date, inter-institutional agreements (IIAs) have been signed with the following universities: RegionLandUniversität Sub-Saharan AfricaGhanaUniversity of Cape Coast UgandaMakerere University EthiopiaMekelle University Western BalkansAlbaniaPolytechnic University of Tirana Ukraine/GeorgienUkraineLviv Polytechnic National University GeorgiaIvane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University GeorgiaIlia State University

When carrying out externally funded research projects, care must be taken to ensure that only expenditure that is necessary to achieve the project objective - taking into account the budgetary principle of efficiency and economy - may be incurred. Which expenses are covered by this is usually determined by the approval in conjunction with the specific cost and financing plan of the funding application and the funding guidelines of the respective program. Please note that the information you provide in the project application is the basis for the approval of funds and forms the framework for the subsequent use of the funds during project implementation. Expenditure expressly rejected by the donor may not be incurred under any circumstances. In the case of expenditure that only becomes necessary in the course of project implementation and for which there is no approval within the framework of the existing financing plan, consultation with the donor is required in all cases. In order to avoid later complaints during audits by the donor, you should have such expenditure approved in writing. Who is it suitable for? Employees can use ESS. Responsibility Responsibility for the SAP FIORI apps is regulated as follows: The HR department is responsible for the content-related operation as well as access and the provision of training. Erasmus+ enables all employees of the University of Kassel to undertake further education and training abroad. On this page you will find important information on the requirements and funding for these so-called staff mobilities for further education and training (STT) as well as a checklist for planning and carrying out your stay. General information about the Erasmus+ program can be found here. Please note our new application deadline of at least 10 weeks prior to the start of the stay. • All employees who are in an employment relationship (regular employment contract; teaching assignment) with the University of Kassel are eligible for funding • The stay takes place as part of a business trip; educational vacations are excluded from Erasmus+ funding • Funding may be granted again no earlier than 24 months after the last funded mobility period • Planned stay takes place in an Erasmus+ program country • In principle, all measures that meet the program requirements are eligible for funding • Language courses (all levels; starting with A1), IF the target language (usually English) is part of professional communication in the workplace AND the course comprises at least 20 hours per week AND the target language is spoken as a first language in the host country • Staff training weeks with an activity and/or internationalization focus • Workshops related to work and/or internationalization • Work shadow

When carrying out externally funded research projects, care must be taken to ensure that only expenditure that is necessary to achieve the project objective - taking into account the budgetary principle of efficiency and economy - may be incurred. Which expenses are covered by this is usually determined by the approval in conjunction with the specific cost and financing plan of the funding application and the funding guidelines of the respective program. Please note that the information you provide in the project application is the basis for the approval of funds and forms the framework for the subsequent use of the funds during project implementation. Expenditure expressly rejected by the donor may not be incurred under any circumstances. In the case of expenditure that only becomes necessary in the course of project implementation and for which there is no approval within the framework of the existing financing plan, consultation with the donor is required in all cases. In order to avoid later complaints during audits by the donor, you should have such expenditure approved in writing. If it is not clear from an expenditure receipt why the procurement/travel etc. was necessary for the project or to achieve the project objective, a brief explanation should be included on the expenditure receipt. top5.title: Consumers and agroforestry systems - FB11AGRAR - Uni Kassel
top5.opening: Consumers and agroforestry systems - FB11AGRAR - Uni Kassel Consumers and agroforestry systems Consumer preferences for agroforestry systems and their products: the example of orchards in Germany Funding Self funded PhD student Duration of project April 2022 - March 2025 Summary Orchards are habitats with a high level of biodiversity. However, developments in recent decades show that despite their ecological importance, political support and the work of orchard initiatives, stocks in Germany continue to decline. Against this background, the aim of the research work is to show ways in which the value of orchards can be increased through improved consumer communication. In order to better understand the purchasing decisions of consumers, it is determined which perceptions and preferences are related to orchard fruit products and how orchard fruit products should be communicated in order to achieve a willingness to buy among consumers, even at higher product prices. The following questions will be answered • What do consumers understand by orchard fruit? What associations do they have with orchard fruit? • What preferences and what willingness to pay do they have for orchard fruit products (apple juice) and what factors influence them? • What are the potential buyer segments for orchard fruit products? How do they differ? top5.opening: Agenda Future-Oriented Consumer Research - FB05 - Uni Kassel Agenda Future-Oriented Consumer Research Initiated by the spokesperson of the coordination committee of the Bundesnetzwerk Verbraucherforschung (Federal Network for Consumer Research), the Research Unit of Sociological Theory at University of Kassel is organizing an agenda process for future-oriented consumer research. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection and based on a resolution of the German Bundestag. As a continuous discussion and work process, the agenda development will extend over a period of 18 months (07/2023 to 12/2024). In a series of six workshops at different locations - with the involvement of expertise from the Federal Network for Consumer Research and beyond - the content of consumer science is to be reviewed and impulses for a future reorientation are to be provided in the form of a final, collaboratively produced white paper. Following a kick-off workshop in late summer, a focused workshop or conference event will be held each quarter. Topics include sustainability, digitalization, social/material (property) rights, professionalization and responsibility. judged.title: SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) - ITS - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) Overview 1. basic information Field of application EVER is used for the electronic processing of incoming invoices. Invoices are recorded, checked and digitally archived in the system, replacing paper-based invoice processing. Who is it suitable for? EVER is relevant for employees who are involved in invoice processing (checking), ordering or approval. Students and lecturers are only indirectly affected if they are involved in procurement processes. Responsibility The organizational responsibility lies with the financial administration. Technical operation is carried out by the IT Service Center 2. brief description Description EVER stands for "Electronic Processing of Incoming Invoices". The aim is transparent, audit-proof and efficient invoice processing. The invoices are stored digitally in SAP using the XSuite software, where they are pre-entered by the accountants and forwarded to the reviewers and approvers via workflow. Processing can take place in SAP or the web-based XFLOW solution. Alternatives Paper-based invoice processing is no longer planned. 3. main functions Functions • Digital invoice receipt: Central recording of all incoming invoices. • Workflow control: Invoices are automatically forwarded to the responsible processor. • Checking and approval: Factual and arithmetical checks are carried out directly in the system. • Archiving: All invoices are stored in an audit-proof manner. • Access options: Processing either via SAP Business Work

top5.opening: Open Access Journal Articles - UB - Uni Kassel Open Access Journal Articles Many OA journals charge article fees (article processing charges) to publish an article. They can be paid from the OA Publication Fund, if the conditions mentioned here are met. We make available a copy of the funded articles in a collection on the KOBRA publication server. We are happy to answer any questions that you may have. The following conditions must be met if the article fees are going to be paid from our fund: • The article must appear in a purely OA journal with a quality assurance procedure that is recognised in the relevant discipline (normally a peer review). We check this by ensuring that the journal is listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ). Any articles in journals, which are not listed there, will only be supported from the fund in exceptional cases, provided that serious quality assurance has been clearly proven and any fraudulent background to the publishing house can be unequivocally ruled out. • In the case of journals published by MDPI, the journal must also be included on a subject-specific list (see below). • The publication fee for an article may not exceed a net figure of EUR 2,000 (plus 19% VAT). top5.opening: Open Access Monographs - UB - Uni Kassel Open Access Monographs Even if print editions continue to be the standard form when it comes to book publications, e-books have now become largely established as parallel options. More and more publishing houses also offer Open Access availability for e-books and charges are made for this. Since mid-2021 we subsidize Open Access fees for books from our Publication Fund, provided that particular conditions are met. We make available a copy of the funded books in a collection on the KOBRA publication server. We are happy to answer any questions that you may have. Amount of subsidies • Open Access monographs can be proportionately subsidised up to a maximum gross figure of EUR 4,000 (incl. VAT). judged.title: SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) - ITS - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) Overview 1. basic information Field of application EVER is used for the electronic processing of incoming invoices. Invoices are recorded, checked and digitally archived in the system, replacing paper-based invoice processing. Who is it suitable for? EVER is relevant for employees who are involved in invoice processing (checking), ordering or approval. Students and lecturers are only indirectly affected if they are involved in procurement processes. Responsibility The organizational responsibility lies with the financial administration. Technical operation is carried out by the IT Service Center 2. brief description Description EVER stands for "Electronic Processing of Incoming Invoices". The aim is transparent, audit-proof and efficient invoice processing. The invoices are stored digitally in SAP using the XSuite software, where they are pre-entered by the accountants and forwarded to the reviewers and approvers via workflow. Processing can take place in SAP or the web-based XFLOW solution. Alternatives Paper-based invoice processing is no longer planned. 3. main functions Functions • Digital invoice receipt: Central recording of all incoming invoices. • Workflow control: Invoices are automatically forwarded to the responsible processor. • Checking and approval: Factual and arithmetical checks are carried out directly in the system. • Archiving: All invoices are stored in an audit-proof manner. • Access options: Processing either via SAP Business Work

judged.title: 4. project implementation - INTERN - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: 4. project implementation - INTERN - Uni Kassel 4. project implementation The content on this page was translated automatically. When carrying out externally funded research projects, care must be taken to ensure that only expenditure that is necessary to achieve the project objective - taking into account the budgetary principle of efficiency and economy - may be incurred. Which expenses are covered by this is usually determined by the approval in conjunction with the specific cost and financing plan of the funding application and the funding guidelines of the respective program. Please note that the information you provide in the project application is the basis for the approval of funds and forms the framework for the subsequent use of the funds during project implementation. Expenditure expressly rejected by the donor may not be incurred under any circumstances. In the case of expenditure that only becomes necessary in the course of project implementation and for which there is no approval within the framework of the existing financing plan, consultation with the donor is required in all cases. In order to avoid later complaints during audits by the donor, you should have such expenditure approved in writing. If it is not clear from an expenditure receipt why the procurement/travel etc. was necessary for the project or to achieve the project objective, a brief explanation should be included on the expenditure receipt. top5.opening: How to cover expenses - EECS - Uni Kassel How to cover expenses What you need to know before applying to the FUSE program The monthly costs to be covered by each student are approximately 1,000 EURO for: • at least 650 €/month for living (including rent, food, books etc.) • Rent: ~ 300 EURO - 450 EURO • Healthcare: ~ 100 EURO • Food: ~ 198 EURO (varies depending on individual lifestyle) • Working materials: ~ 50 EURO - 100 EURO • Recreation, culture and sports: ~ 65 EURO (varies depending on individual lifestyle) • Semester fees are approximately 392 EURO per semester. Possible ways to cover the required expenses: The complete expenses (including accomodation, semester contribution, food, health insurance, public transport etc.) for four semesters amount to about 30,000 EURO. Clearly, the exact sum depends on the individual way of living, price levels etc. It is important that you are able to cover these expenses. German foreign authorities do not grant student visa without proof of sufficient financial means. The proof may be provided by ONE of the following: • disclosure of parents income and assets OR • a binding declaration of the parents to the German consular representative or the corresponding office that they will pay the expenses of the student OR • the placement of a deposit in a frozen bank account in Germany OR • a proof of a scholarship (apply e.g. at the DAAD) OR • the annually renewed placement of a bank letter of guarantee with a bank in Germany. Currently, the receipts to be reimbursed must be sent to the Finance Department via a paper-based process. In order to minimize the administrative effort with the reimbursements and to achieve a higher level of satisfaction for all parties involved, a portal solution is to be developed for the paper-based process and implemented step by step. For this purpose, a target concept was created as part of the university-wide project "Simplify and Omit" and presented on July 13, 2023 at the final event of the above-mentioned project. The portal solution is to be implemented by the end of this year. Close coordination with the faculties and the ITS is necessary for successful implementation. top5.title: How to cover Expenses - EECS - Uni Kassel
top5.opening: How to cover Expenses - EECS - Uni Kassel How to cover Expenses The monthly costs to be covered by each student are approximately 1,000 EURO for: • Rent: ~ 300 EURO - 450 EURO • Healthcare: ~ 100 EURO • Food: ~ 198 EURO (varies depending on individual lifestyle) • Working materials: ~ 50 EURO - 100 EURO • Recreation, culture and sports: ~ 65 EURO (varies depending on individual lifestyle) Semester fees are approximately 392 EURO per semester. Possible ways to cover the required expenses: The complete expenses (including accomodation, semester contribution, food, health insurance, public transport etc.) for four semesters amount to about 30,000 EURO. Clearly, the exact sum depends on the individual way of living, price levels etc. It is important that you are able to cover these expenses. German foreign authorities do not grant student visa without proof of sufficient financial means. The proof may be provided by ONE of the following: • disclosure of parents income and assets OR • a binding declaration of the parents to the German consular representative or the corresponding office that they will pay the expenses of the student OR • the placement of a deposit in a frozen bank account in Germany OR • a proof of a scholarship OR • the annually renewed placement of a bank letter of guarantee with a bank in Germany. Furthermore, you must show evidence that you have a health insurance to cover corresponding expenses in Germany. judged.title: SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) - ITS - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP EVER (Electronic Invoice Receipt) Overview 1. basic information Field of application EVER is used for the electronic processing of incoming invoices. Invoices are recorded, checked and digitally archived in the system, replacing paper-based invoice processing. Who is it suitable for? EVER is relevant for employees who are involved in invoice processing (checking), ordering or approval. Students and lecturers are only indirectly affected if they are involved in procurement processes. Responsibility The organizational responsibility lies with the financial administration. Technical operation is carried out by the IT Service Center 2. brief description Description EVER stands for "Electronic Processing of Incoming Invoices". The aim is transparent, audit-proof and efficient invoice processing. The invoices are stored digitally in SAP using the XSuite software, where they are pre-entered by the accountants and forwarded to the reviewers and approvers via workflow. Processing can take place in SAP or the web-based XFLOW solution. Alternatives Paper-based invoice processing is no longer planned. 3. main functions Functions • Digital invoice receipt: Central recording of all incoming invoices. • Workflow control: Invoices are automatically forwarded to the responsible processor. • Checking and approval: Factual and arithmetical checks are carried out directly in the system. • Archiving: All invoices are stored in an audit-proof manner. • Access options: Processing either via SAP Business Work

top5.title: SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) - ITS - Uni Kassel
top5.opening: SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) Overview Directly to: 1. basic information Field of application The system enables the digital processing of business trip requests as well as the creation and submission of travel expense reports via the SAP Employee Self-Service (ESS). Who is it suitable for? Employees can use ESS. Responsibility Responsibility for the SAP FIORI apps is regulated as follows: The HR department is responsible for the content-related operation as well as access and the provision of training. The technical operation is ensured by ITS or HeHRZ Darmstadt. 2. short description Description The SAP ESS portal offers an end-to-end workflow for the approval of business trip requests and travel expense reports. The processes are digitized and handled via the web browser - including uploading evidence and automatic form creation. Since summer 2025, ESS has been accessed entirely via SAP FIORI. Alternatives There are currently no technical alternatives available. 3. main functions Functions • Create business trip request • Workflow & approval: multi-stage process - technical and financial review, automatic commitment of funds. • Travel expense report: transfer of application data, entry of actual costs, upload of receipts, selection of domestic and international scheme. • Status overview: Accessible overviews of travel requests, expense reports and their processing status. Possibility to correct, delete or change under certain conditions 4th deployment scenario Practical examples

top5.opening: Document management system - ITS - Uni Kassel Document management system Overview Directly to: 1. basic information Field of application The document management system (DMS) at the University of Kassel is used for the central administration of electronic files and documents (e.g. contracts, invoices, applications) as well as digital, process-oriented transaction processing in all administrative areas. The aim is to gradually replace paper-based processes with electronic workflows in order to increase efficiency and transparency. Who is it suitable for? The DMS is being introduced step by step together with the specialist departments responsible for the respective processes. As the system supports numerous processes at the interfaces between the central university administration, the departmental administrations and other organizational units, the majority of employees will work with the DMS in the future. Access rights to processes and documents are based on the respective field of activity and the specific tasks of the employees. Responsibility The DMS is being introduced as part of the project "Introduction of digital document-supported transaction processing" and is managed jointly by the IT Service Centre (ITS) and the Department of Human Resources and Organization. The DMS is managed by the ITS of the University of Kassel. Further information can be found on the DMS project website. 2. brief description Description The DMS of the University of Kassel is a browser-based software solution that enables the database-supported management of files and documents

top5.title: Open Access Journal Articles - UB - Uni Kassel
top5.opening: Open Access Journal Articles - UB - Uni Kassel Open Access Journal Articles Many OA journals charge article fees (article processing charges) to publish an article. They can be paid from the OA Publication Fund, if the conditions mentioned here are met. We make available a copy of the funded articles in a collection on the KOBRA publication server. We are happy to answer any questions that you may have. The following conditions must be met if the article fees are going to be paid from our fund: • The article must appear in a purely OA journal with a quality assurance procedure that is recognised in the relevant discipline (normally a peer review). We check this by ensuring that the journal is listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ). Any articles in journals, which are not listed there, will only be supported from the fund in exceptional cases, provided that serious quality assurance has been clearly proven and any fraudulent background to the publishing house can be unequivocally ruled out. • In the case of journals published by MDPI, the journal must also be included on a subject-specific list (see below). • The publication fee for an article may not exceed a net figure of EUR 2,000 (plus 19% VAT). Higher fees can be subsidized proportionately up to this amount from 2022. The costs exceeding this amount are to be paid by the authors. judged.opening: Procurement of end devices - ITS - Uni Kassel Procurement of end devices The content on this page was translated automatically. Back to overview Information on the IT framework agreement We are pleased to inform you that we have concluded a framework agreement with Bechtle as of November 1, 2023. This contract covers the provision of PCs, notebooks, docking stations and monitors for our Employees. Please note that according to the terms of the contract, all orders must be placed exclusively via our WPS system (Web Procurement System). This ensures that all orders are processed smoothly and that the agreed conditions of the framework agreement are adhered to. Registration in the WPS system is only possible if you have already attended the relevant training course. Dates can be found at https://veranstaltungen.uni-kassel.de. If you have any queries, please contact the finance department directly. Areas that are supported by the IT Service Center (e.g. the University Administration) and those that wish to use a UKC (UniKasselClient) order hardware using a corresponding procurement form. You can send the completed form to the IT Service Center by e-mail chain via the supervisor and, if necessary, additionally via the cost center manager to the following e-mail address: it-beschaffung[at]uni-kassel[dot]de The available models and prices can be viewed under the"Offers" tab. judged.opening: Accessibility - UNI Accessibility This page contains automatically translated content. EU Directive 2016/2102 requires public sector bodies to ensure that their websites and mobile applications are accessible. We would like to take this opportunity to inform you about how and when we checked the accessibility of our website, what weaknesses still exist and what improvements we are planning. Scope of the declaration This declaration applies to all websites that are offered in the central web CMS system of the University of Kassel. Standard applied The design of accessibility is based on the requirements of the Hessian Ordinance on Barrier-free Information Technology of September 16, 2019 and the Ordinance on the Creation of Barrier-free Information Technology in accordance with the Disability Equality Act (Barrier-free Information Technology Ordinance - BITV 2.0). Current status The website of the University of Kassel has been checked several times for accessibility and is considered to be accessible with restrictions. The check was carried out as a self-assessment with support from third parties. top5.opening: Sitemap News Detail - FORSCHUNG - Uni Kassel 01.04.2021 The Timber Footprint of the German Bioeconomy - State of the Art and Past Development @CESR The article gives a comprehensive overview of the roundwood equivalents (RE) consumed in the German bioeconomy from Germany and abroad between 1995 and 2015, i.e., the Timber Footprint of final Consumption (TFP<sub>con</sub>). The calculation is based on an adapted version of Exiobase 3.4. The sustainability of roundwood procurement for the TFP<sub>con</sub> is assessed. A systematic embedding of the tree compartments considered in the TFP in the context of national forest inventories and material flow analysis is presented. The results show that, in 2015, the total volume of the TFP<sub>con</sub> of Germany is 90 Mm<sup>3</sup> (slightly above the 1995 level) and is composed of 61% coniferous and 39% non-coniferous wood. Germany is strongly dependent on roundwood sourced from abroad and thus was a net importer of RE in 2015. Among the 17 countries with the largest supply of RE for the TFP<sub>con</sub>, around one third very likely include large shares of roundwood procured from deforestation or clear-cutting. The self-sufficiency rate in 2015 was only 76%. It would be possible to increase domestic roundwood production by 8–41% (mainly in the hardwood sector) without exceeding the sustainability limits as defined in the WEHAM scenarios. judged.title: SAP WPS (goods ordering system) - ITS - Uni Kassel
judged.opening: SAP WPS (goods ordering system) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP WPS (goods ordering system) Overview Directly to: 1. basic information Field of application WPS (Web Procurement System) serves as a supplementary procurement tool to SAP and is used at universities to enable standardized, efficient and transparent ordering processes - especially for IT end devices - via a web browser. Who is it suitable for? This system is available to university employees with a corresponding training certificate - especially employees who have to order hardware or services via university framework contracts. Responsibility The IT Service Center provides access and operation of the system. The personnel development and finance departments are responsible for activation and training. 2. brief description Description WPS is a browser-based add-on tool for SAP that is used to process orders - especially for end devices - centrally and digitally. It ensures compliance with framework agreements and enables simple user guidance through the ordering processes. Alternatives 3. main functions Functions • Orders in the framework agreement: End devices such as PCs, notebooks and monitors can be ordered via WPS - always at the agreed conditions. • Access control via training: WPS accounts can only be assigned after successful participation in SAP MM training. • Selection of offers and accessories: Models and price options can be viewed in the system under the "Offers" tab. Additional equipment such as RAM or larger hard disks can be specifically selected. 4th deployment scenario Practical

judged.title: Visa, entry and residence issues - UNI
judged.opening: Visa, entry and residence issues - UNI Visa, entry and residence issues Information for international students and prospective students The University of Kassel does not issue visas. We merely provide you with information about the applicable regulations. Please always check the current regulations on the official website of the Federal Foreign Office, as the legal framework can change. We recommend that you start your visa application early to avoid delays. Overview Contact us The International Office will be happy to answer any questions you may have. Consultation hours: Tuesday and Thursday 1-3pm and by appointment Who needs a visa? EU/EEA citizens (including Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway) do not require a visa or residence permit. All other nationals (so-called third countries) must generally apply for a long-term student visa before entering Germany. Exceptions: Citizens of the following countries can enter Germany without a visa and apply for a residence permit within 90 days of entering the country: • Australia • Canada • Israel • Japan • New Zealand • South Korea • Switzerland • United Kingdom (UK) • USA Citizens of Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco and San Marino may also apply for a residence permit after entering the country, but may not work until the application has been approved. The University of Kassel allocates its own funds from the university budget to research projects (see Central Research Funding). The vast majority of research activities, however, is funded by third-party grants. These third-party funds are provided by public institutions (BMFTR, DFG, the EU, foundations, DAAD, etc.), industry, or through donations. A basic distinction is made between grant-funded projects, contract research (R&D projects), and service projects. The Third-Party Funding Management Group at the University of Kassel serves as a liaison between funding agencies on the one hand and the recipients of these funds in the academic departments and research institutions on the other. top5.opening: Further training abroad for staff members - UNI Further training abroad for staff members This page contains automatically translated content. Erasmus+ enables all employees of the University of Kassel to undertake further education and training abroad. On this page you will find important information on the requirements and funding for these so-called staff mobilities for further education and training (STT) as well as a checklist for planning and carrying out your stay. General information about the Erasmus+ program can be found here. Please note our new application deadline of at least 10 weeks prior to the start of the stay. • All employees who are in an employment relationship (regular employment contract; teaching assignment) with the University of Kassel are eligible for funding • The stay takes place as part of a business trip; educational vacations are excluded from Erasmus+ funding • Funding may be granted again no earlier than 24 months after the last funded mobility period • Planned stay takes place in an Erasmus+ program country • In principle, all measures that meet the program requirements are eligible for funding • Language courses (all levels; starting with A1), IF the target language (usually English) is part of professional communication in the workplace AND the course comprises at least 20 hours per week AND the target language is spoken as a first language in the host country • Staff training weeks with an activity and/or internationalization focus • Workshops related to work and/or internationalization • Work shadow

top5.title: Mobility Fund for scientists with family responsibilities - HOCHSCHULVERWALTUNG
top5.opening: Mobility Fund for scientists with family responsibilities - HOCHSCHULVERWALTUNG Mobility Fund for scientists with family responsibilities To improve conditions for balancing family and academic life, the university has set up a mobility fund for academics, especially early-career researchers with family responsibilities. The fund can be used to subsidize mobility costs relating to family responsibilities to reconcile conference attendance, business trips, research stays abroad, etc. with family responsibilities. The prerequisite is the necessity of taking children under the age of 16 and people involved in childcare (e.g., relatives) on business trips and/or additional childcare or nursing costs at the place of residence. A grant of up to 250 euros can be requested per child or relative. Funding within the framework of third-party funded projects must take place in consultation with the Family Welcome Service. Applications must be submitted via the Family Welcome Service of the Equal Opportunities Office. Mobility Fund Form Contact Family Welcome and Dual Career Service Mönchebergstr. 19 34109 Kassel +49 561 804-2813 familywelcomeservice[at]uni-kassel[dot]de

Locations of the new bicycle parking facilities (opens enlarged image) News from the mobility & transport sector New lockable bicycle boxes at HoPla • For the time being, three bicycle boxes have been completed at Hopla; these are located at the Institute of Music, the Engineering Sciences I building and the K10 building. A further box will be installed in Georg-Foster-Straße once the construction work has been completed. top5.opening: SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP ESS (Business Travel Management) Overview Directly to: 1. basic information Field of application The system enables the digital processing of business trip requests as well as the creation and submission of travel expense reports via the SAP Employee Self-Service (ESS). Who is it suitable for? Employees can use ESS. Responsibility Responsibility for the SAP FIORI apps is regulated as follows: The HR department is responsible for the content-related operation as well as access and the provision of training. The technical operation is ensured by ITS or HeHRZ Darmstadt. 2. short description Description The SAP ESS portal offers an end-to-end workflow for the approval of business trip requests and travel expense reports. The processes are digitized and handled via the web browser - including uploading evidence and automatic form creation. Since summer 2025, ESS has been accessed entirely via SAP FIORI. Alternatives There are currently no technical alternatives available. 3. main functions Functions • Create business trip request • Workflow & approval: multi-stage process - technical and financial review, automatic commitment of funds. • Travel expense report: transfer of application data, entry of actual costs, upload of receipts, selection of domestic and international scheme. • Status overview: Accessible overviews of travel requests, expense reports and their processing status. Possibility to correct, delete or change under certain conditions 4th deployment scenario Practical examples

top5.opening: Open Access Journal Articles - UB - Uni Kassel Open Access Journal Articles Many OA journals charge article fees (article processing charges) to publish an article. They can be paid from the OA Publication Fund, if the conditions mentioned here are met. We make available a copy of the funded articles in a collection on the KOBRA publication server. We are happy to answer any questions that you may have. The following conditions must be met if the article fees are going to be paid from our fund: • The article must appear in a purely OA journal with a quality assurance procedure that is recognised in the relevant discipline (normally a peer review). We check this by ensuring that the journal is listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ). Any articles in journals, which are not listed there, will only be supported from the fund in exceptional cases, provided that serious quality assurance has been clearly proven and any fraudulent background to the publishing house can be unequivocally ruled out. • In the case of journals published by MDPI, the journal must also be included on a subject-specific list (see below). • The publication fee for an article may not exceed a net figure of EUR 2,000 (plus 19% VAT). Higher fees can be subsidized proportionately up to this amount from 2022. The costs exceeding this amount are to be paid by the authors. General information about systems Assets are tangible or intangible assets that remain permanently in the business and are necessary for its operation. A distinction is made between intangible assets (e.g. software) and tangible assets (e.g. machines, PCs, vehicles, etc.). What are the value limits? The account assignment manual of the state of Hesse specifies the following value limits: • Low-value assets (GWG): € 150.00 - € 410.00 net/device Incidental purchase costs (e.g. freight, commissioning) are to be added to the purchase price of the asset, discounts and rebates are to be deducted. • Equipment: > € 410.00 net/device Ancillary purchase costs (e.g. freight, commissioning) are to be added to the purchase price of the asset, discounts and rebates are to be deducted. • Expenses: maintenance, temporary licenses, servicing, etc. If you have any questions, you can contact the asset accounting clerk at any time (Tel. -2227). Order process (procurement) Procurement information The basis for every order/procurement is the procurement regulations of the University of Kassel. The goods ordered may belong to the following categories, depending on price or product type: • Consumables/equipment • GWG Low-value assets, independently usable equipment with a value of € 250.00 to € 800.00 (plus VAT) • Equipment Purchases from € 800.01 must fulfill the following two requirements: 1. it must be an independently usable device. 2. the net unit price must be € 800.01 or more. The allocation must be entered during the ordering process. In principle, 3 quotations must be obtained, with the exception of framework agreement partners. Framework contract partners are suppliers from whom the contractually agreed products must be purchased. If you want to order a product for which a framework agreement exists, you must order this product exclusively from the framework agreement partner Procedure 1. orders must be placed by the cost center representative (usually the head of the department). Back to overview Information on the IT framework agreement We are pleased to inform you that we have concluded a framework agreement with Bechtle as of November 1, 2023. This contract covers the provision of PCs, notebooks, docking stations and monitors for our Employees. Please note that according to the terms of the contract, all orders must be placed exclusively via our WPS system (Web Procurement System). This ensures that all orders are processed smoothly and that the agreed conditions of the framework agreement are adhered to. Registration in the WPS system is only possible if you have already attended the relevant training course. Dates can be found at https://veranstaltungen.uni-kassel.de. If you have any queries, please contact the finance department directly. top5.title: SAP WPS (goods ordering system) - ITS - Uni Kassel
top5.opening: SAP WPS (goods ordering system) - ITS - Uni Kassel SAP WPS (goods ordering system) Overview Directly to: 1. basic information Field of application WPS (Web Procurement System) serves as a supplementary procurement tool to SAP and is used at universities to enable standardized, efficient and transparent ordering processes - especially for IT end devices - via a web browser. Who is it suitable for? This system is available to university employees with a corresponding training certificate - especially employees who have to order hardware or services via university framework contracts. Responsibility The IT Service Center provides access and operation of the system. The personnel development and finance departments are responsible for activation and training. 2. brief description Description WPS is a browser-based add-on tool for SAP that is used to process orders - especially for end devices - centrally and digitally. It ensures compliance with framework agreements and enables simple user guidance through the ordering processes. Alternatives 3. main functions Functions • Orders in the framework agreement: End devices such as PCs, notebooks and monitors can be ordered via WPS - always at the agreed conditions. • Access control via training: WPS accounts can only be assigned after successful participation in SAP MM training. • Selection of offers and accessories: Models and price options can be viewed in the system under the "Offers" tab. Additional equipment such as RAM or larger hard disks can be specifically selected. 4th deployment scenario Practical
